## The four SAP reporting regimes and the seams between them

The four SAP reporting regimes and the seams between them is a domain on the board; board tier B, documented channel and capability, programme role indicated but not yet nailed to a primary source; dates 1987-12-04; axes C1 A3 D3; 6 connections.

In one line: analysis.

### What it is

There is no single United States statute on special access programs. There are four parallel regimes plus covert action, and the differences between them are where a program can live. (1) DoD - 10 U.S.C. 119: annual report by 1 March, new-program notice by 1 February, 14-day declassification notice, 30-day report-and-wait, all to six defense committees; the Secretary may waive the reports on a national-security determination, in which case the information goes only to the chairman and ranking minority member of each. (2) NNSA - 50 U.S.C. 2426: identical structure to the defense committees, but the Administrator may additionally waive the 30-day report-and-wait itself. (3) Every other agency - 50 U.S.C. 3348: identical structure, but reporting runs to 'congressional oversight committees' expressly including House Oversight and Senate Homeland Security, and the waiver does not narrow the audience. (4) The Intelligence Community - 50 U.S.C. 3091a and ICD 906: no annual statutory deadline and no waiver at all, but semiannual briefings on every program, a prohibition on establishment before notification, a funding cutoff since December 2024, and a prohibition on transferring capabilities out of a CAP into a SAP without notice since December 2024. Set beside each other, the ranking is unambiguous: the weakest reporting regime in the United States government belongs to the Department of Defense, and it is weakest precisely at the point where the Secretary decides how much to tell the committees. Two structural seams follow. The first is between regimes: a capability transferred from an IC controlled access program to a DoD special access program changes which statute governs it and which committees see it - the manoeuvre Congress prohibited prospectively in December 2024, three decades after the alleged conduct. The second is around all four: ICD 906 section C.3 records that none of them applies to 'special access programs under the purview of the National Security Council, such as covert action', which are governed only by 50 U.S.C. 3093 and its Gang of Eight.

### The board's reading

Where a program could sit, and what changes when it moves. There are five distinct legal environments, and the practical differences between them are the map of where concealment is easiest. (1) A DoD special access program: reports to six defense committees, waivable to eight to twelve members by the Secretary's own determination. (2) An NNSA special access program: same committees, and the Administrator may additionally waive the 30-day advance notice itself, so a program can begin with no committee ever having been told in advance - and NNSA material is Restricted Data, born classified by operation of the Atomic Energy Act rather than by an original classification authority, so a presidential declassification order operating on E.O. 13526 information does not reach it. (3) A non-DoD, non-NNSA, non-IC agency special access program: reports to House Oversight and Senate Homeland Security among others, and the waiver does not narrow the audience - the strongest of the SAP regimes, and the one covering DHS, NASA, Justice and Commerce. (4) An IC Controlled Access Program: no waiver at all, semiannual briefings, a funding cutoff since December 2024 and, since December 2024, a prohibition on transferring a capability out into a special access program without notice. (5) A National Security Council covert action program: outside all four SAP regimes by the express terms of ICD 906 section C.3, governed only by 50 U.S.C. 3093. The seam that matters is between (4) and (1). Before 23 December 2024 there was no statutory requirement to notify anyone when a capability moved from an IC controlled access program into a DoD special access program, and the move changes both the governing statute and the committees entitled to know. Congress closed that door prospectively in section 6603 of Public Law 118-159 - and left it ajar with an exception for transfers 'necessary to maintain access in the event of an organizational restructuring', a determination the transferring official makes for himself.

### Why it holds its tier

Re-graded B on a global pass (rank 203 of 1159, score 45). 6 connections, 1 of them custody/funding/programmatic. Axes C1/A3/D3.

### The claims on the record

- **Tier 1 documented.** Four separate statutes govern SAP-type reporting: 10 U.S.C. 119 (DoD), 50 U.S.C. 2426 (NNSA), 50 U.S.C. 3348 (all other non-IC agencies) and 50 U.S.C. 3091a (IC controlled access programs). Source: 10 U.S.C. 119; 50 U.S.C. 2426, 3348, 3091a
- **Tier 1 documented.** Four statutes, each with a different addressee. DoD: 10 U.S.C. 119 (defense committees; annual 1 Mar; waiver in (e) collapsing to chairman + ranking member). NNSA: 50 U.S.C. 2426 (congressional defense committees; annual 1 Feb; identical waiver). All other non-IC agencies: 50 U.S.C. 3348 (congressional oversight committees; annual 1 Feb; waiver that does NOT reduce the audience). IC: 50 U.S.C. 3091a (intelligence committees + both Appropriations + the four congressional leaders; semiannual briefings; no waiver at all). Source: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2023-title50/html/USCODE-2023-title50-chap45-subchapIII-sec3348.htm
- **Tier 1 documented.** Of the four regimes, only 10 U.S.C. 119(e)(2) and 50 U.S.C. 2426(e)(2) narrow the recipient of waived information to the chairman and ranking minority member; 50 U.S.C. 3348(e)(2) keeps the full oversight committees, and 50 U.S.C. 3091a has no waiver provision at all. Source: Comparison of 10 U.S.C. 119(e), 50 U.S.C. 2426(e), 50 U.S.C. 3348(e) and 50 U.S.C. 3091a
- **Tier 1 documented.** Only 50 U.S.C. 3091a carries a funding prohibition tied to notification, added by section 6602 of Public Law 118-159 on 23 December 2024. Source: 50 U.S.C. 3091a(c)
- **Tier 1 documented.** The seams are written into the statutes. 50 U.S.C. 3348(g)(2)(B) removes DoD, NNSA and every IC element from its own coverage. 50 U.S.C. 3091a(d)(3) defines its subject by reference to ICD 906. ICD 906 section C.3 in turn removes from its own coverage every SAP created by the Secretaries of State, Defense, Energy or Homeland Security or the Attorney General, and 'special access programs under the purview of the National Security Council, such as covert action.' Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20250112183207/https://www.dni.gov/files/documents/ICD/ICD-906-Controlled-Access-Programs.pdf
- **Tier 3 stated inference.** A program moved between the DoD and IC regimes changes both its governing statute and its reporting audience, and before 23 December 2024 no statute required notice of the move. That is a documented, lawful, unnotified route by which a program's oversight history can be broken. Reasoning: the prohibition added by Pub. L. 118-159 sec. 6603 did not exist before that date and operates prospectively. Source: 50 U.S.C. 3091a(b)(2) and its 2024 enactment date
- **Tier 3 stated inference.** Composed, the four regimes leave two seams with no annual census obligation running to a full committee: (i) a DoD program under a 119(e) waiver, whose content goes only to chairs and ranking members and whose annual report requirement additionally sunset on 31 Dec 2021 under Pub. L. 114-328 sec. 1061; and (ii) anything protected by ACCM rather than SAP controls, which no statute names. Covert action under 50 U.S.C. 3093 is a third, separately governed channel. Reasoning stated from the four statutes plus 32 CFR 117.3. Source: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2023-title10/html/USCODE-2023-title10-subtitleA-partI-chap2-sec119.htm

## GAO/NSIAD-88-152 - Special Access Programs: DOD Criteria and Procedures for Creating Them Need Improvement

GAO/NSIAD-88-152 - Special Access Programs: DOD Criteria and Procedures for Creating Them Need Improvement is a document on the board; board tier B, documented channel and capability, programme role indicated but not yet nailed to a primary source; dates 1988-05-24; axes C1 A1 D1; 6 connections.

In one line: Unclassified summary to congressional committees, B-230522, 24 May 1988; summary of a classified report of 1 April 1988.

### What it is

GAO reported to the four defence committees under section 1133 of Public Law 100-180 on how the Department of Defense decides to make a programme special access. It found that DoD does not follow its own two criteria, that the definition of a special access programme is not clear inside the department, and that the official required to hold a list of all such programmes does not hold one. The report is the record behind the board's argument that special access status is asserted rather than justified, and it dates the Army's own centralised oversight office to September 1984, ten years before the reform the board carries at dod-sap-reform-1994.

### Why it holds its tier

Re-graded B on a global pass (rank 434 of 1159, score 33). 6 connections, 1 of them custody/funding/programmatic. Axes C1/A1/D1.

### The claims on the record

- **Tier 1 documented.** Creation authority is held by four people: 'Only the three service secretaries and Deputy Under Secretary of Defense for Policy are authorized to establish special access programs.' Source: GAO/NSIAD-88-152, Results in Brief, https://www.gao.gov/assets/nsiad-88-152.pdf
- **Tier 1 documented.** GAO's central finding: 'We found that the Department of Defense does not adequately follow criteria to be used in determining the need to establish programs as special accessrequired. The definition of special accessprograms is not clear within the Department of Defense and, until recently, the oversight role of the Office of the Secretary of Defense in the programs' creation has been limited.' Source: GAO/NSIAD-88-152, transmittal letter, https://www.gao.gov/assets/nsiad-88-152.pdf
- **Tier 1 documented.** Nobody held a list: 'The Deputy Under Secretary of Defense for Policy is required to maintain a listing of all special access programs, but does not do so because of security concerns.' GAO adds that 'the Secretary's Office has no centralized office with cognizance of all special access programs'. Source: GAO/NSIAD-88-152, Results in Brief, https://www.gao.gov/assets/nsiad-88-152.pdf
- **Tier 1 documented.** The Army reform is dated to 1983-84, not 1994: 'A DOD review of Army special access programs in 1983 revealed systemic weaknesses in various management areas, which resulted in establishment of a central oversight office in September 1984.' Source: GAO/NSIAD-88-152, Recommendations section, https://www.gao.gov/assets/nsiad-88-152.pdf
- **Tier 1 documented.** The report is a summary of a classified one and answers a statute: 'This report is an unclassified summary of a classified report that we sent to you on April 1, 1988.' The review 'is in response to section 1133 of Public Law 100-180, which requires that the Comptroller General report to the defense committees on this subject.' Source: GAO/NSIAD-88-152, B-230522, 24 May 1988, transmittal letter, https://www.gao.gov/assets/nsiad-88-152.pdf

## GAO/NSIAD-95-187, Results of a Search for Records Concerning the 1947 Crash Near Roswell

GAO/NSIAD-95-187, Results of a Search for Records Concerning the 1947 Crash Near Roswell is a document on the board; board tier B, documented channel and capability, programme role indicated but not yet nailed to a primary source; dates 1995; axes C2 A1 D3; 6 connections.

In one line: General Accounting Office report, 28 July 1995.

### What it is

The most important single document in this domain and the one that survives any hostile audit. Requested by Rep. Steven H. Schiff after the Defense Department refused to answer him, the General Accounting Office worked the file from March 1994 to June 1995 and reported on 28 July 1995. GAO searched Air Force, Army, Navy, Defense Department, CIA, FBI, NSA, National Security Council and National Archives holdings. Its findings on the record itself are unambiguous and are stated in the government's own auditing language: 'RAAF outgoing messages (from Oct. 1946 through Dec. 1949) were destroyed', and RAAF administrative records from March 1945 through December 1949 were destroyed, and, the sentence this board treats as central, 'The document disposition form does not indicate what organization or person destroyed the records and when or under what authority the records were destroyed.' Federal records are not destroyed without disposition authority; that is the entire premise of the Federal Records Act. GAO also recorded the FBI's 8 July 1947 teletype from Dallas describing the recovery of 'a hexagonal-shaped disc suspended from a large balloon by cable', and the CIA Executive Director's statement that a search against 'Roswell, New Mexico' in all CIA databases produced no documents. Thirty-one years later no accountability review of the destruction has ever been conducted.

### The board's reading

GAO/NSIAD-95-187 is the only place in the entire legacy-era record where an independent arm of the United States government audited the paper trail and reported what it found. The scope was set by Rep. Steven H. Schiff of New Mexico after the Defense Department declined to answer his inquiries. GAO searched Air Force, Army, Navy, Defense Department, CIA, FBI, NSA, National Security Council and National Archives records, and visited multiple National Archives facilities to review Air Force UFO papers and Army Counterintelligence Corps records for 1947-1949. The report's operative findings are three sentences long and have never been rebutted by any agency: RAAF outgoing messages from October 1946 through December 1949 were destroyed; RAAF administrative records from March 1945 through December 1949 were destroyed; and the document disposition form does not indicate what organization or person destroyed the records and when or under what authority the records were destroyed. The Federal Records Act requires a disposition authority for the destruction of federal records. Its absence here is not a filing irregularity, it is the removal of the entire contemporaneous documentary output of a specific installation across precisely the years in question, with no accountable party. GAO also captured two other facts of standing value: the FBI's 8 July 1947 Dallas teletype recording Eighth Air Force's description of a hexagonal disc suspended from a balloon by cable, and the CIA Executive Director's statement that a search against 'Roswell, New Mexico' in all CIA databases produced no documents. Thirty-one years later, no executive-branch review, including AARO's 2024 historical report, has addressed the destruction finding, and no accountability inquiry has been opened.

## The misappropriation allegation: Grusch's ICIG complaint and sworn testimony

The misappropriation allegation: Grusch's ICIG complaint and sworn testimony is a event on the board; board tier A, named in sworn testimony or primary documents as directly inside the programme; dates 2022-05 to 2023-07-26; axes C2 A3 D3; 6 connections.

In one line: May 2022 ICIG urgent-concern complaint; 26 July 2023 sworn testimony to House Oversight.

### What it is

The specific allegation that programme funds were moved into private contractor custody outside congressional oversight has a named source, a date, a legal vehicle and an oath. David Charles Grusch, formerly the National Reconnaissance Office's representative to the Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force and a senior technical adviser on UAP analysis at the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, filed a Disclosure of Urgent Concern and Complaint of Reprisal with the Intelligence Community Inspector General in May 2022, through counsel Charles McCullough III - himself a former Intelligence Community Inspector General. The ICIG found the complaint credible and urgent in July 2022. Grusch then briefed the staffs of the congressional intelligence committees in closed session. On 5 June 2023 he went on the record with Leslie Kean and Ralph Blumenthal in The Debrief, stating: 'Individuals on these UAP programs approached me in my official capacity and disclosed their concerns regarding a multitude of wrongdoings, such as illegal contracting against the Federal Acquisition Regulations and other criminality and the suppression of information across a qualified industrial base and academia.' That sentence is the named mechanism: not a generic accusation of secrecy but a specific claim of procurement fraud - contracting conducted outside the Federal Acquisition Regulation, which is the body of law governing how the government buys things and what the government owns when it has paid. On 26 July 2023 Grusch testified under oath before the Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs of the House Committee on Oversight and Accountability, at a hearing titled 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Implications on National Security, Public Safety, and Government Transparency', alongside Ryan Graves and Commander David Fravor. His written statement records that he was 'informed in the course of my official duties of a multi-decade UAP crash retrieval and reverse engineering program' to which he was denied access, and refers to 'Non-Human Reverse Engineering Programs'; the specific financial detail he declined to give in open session, offering it in a classified setting. Five months later Congress enacted section 1687 of the FY2024 NDAA, barring funds for unreported UAP special access activity and barring UAP-related contractor independent research and development from being an allowable indirect cost. The sequence - complaint, credible-and-urgent finding, closed briefings, sworn testimony, statute naming IR&D - is the strongest documented chain on this board connecting an allegation about money to legislative action about money.

Re-graded A on a global pass (rank 161 of 1159, score 51). 6 connections, 1 of them custody/funding/programmatic, 1 official denial recorded against it. Axes C2/A3/D3.

## A Die-hard Issue: CIA's Role in the Study of UFOs, 1947-1990

A Die-hard Issue: CIA's Role in the Study of UFOs, 1947-1990 is a document on the board; board tier A, named in sworn testimony or primary documents as directly inside the programme; dates 1997; axes C0 A3 D2; 6 connections.

In one line: Gerald K. Haines, CIA Studies in Intelligence, 1997.

### What it is

The CIA's own official history of its involvement with unidentified flying objects, written by NRO historian Gerald K. Haines and published in the Agency's in-house journal Studies in Intelligence in 1997. It is included here as a primary source because it contains admissions no outside researcher could have obtained. It states that Chadwell and Robertson assembled the January 1953 panel; that 'CIA officials wanted knowledge of any Agency interest in the subject of flying saucers carefully restricted, noting not only that the Robertson panel report was classified but also that any mention of CIA sponsorship of the panel was forbidden'; that the panel canvassed mass media, advertising, business clubs, schools and the Disney corporation to carry its message; that 'according to later estimates from CIA officials who worked on the U-2 project and the OXCART project, over half of all UFO reports from the late 1950s through the 1960s were accounted for by manned reconnaissance flights'; and that this 'led the Air Force to make misleading and deceptive statements to the public in order to allay public fears and to protect an extraordinarily sensitive national security project'. An agency of the United States government has therefore stated in writing that the Air Force deceived the American public about unidentified flying objects for national security reasons. The dispute is not about whether the government lies about this subject. It is about what else it was covering.

### Why it holds its tier

Re-graded A on a global pass (rank 94 of 1159, score 65). 9 connections, 0 of them custody/funding/programmatic, 3 official denials recorded against it. Axes C0/A3/D2.

### The claims on the record

- **Tier 1 documented.** 'According to later estimates from CIA officials who worked on the U-2 project and the OXCART (SR-71, or Blackbird) project, over half of all UFO reports from the late 1950s through the 1960s were accounted for by manned reconnaissance flights (namely the U-2) over the United States.' Source: Haines, 'CIA's Role in the Study of UFOs, 1947-90'
- **Tier 1 documented.** 'According to later estimates from CIA officials who worked on the U-2 project and the OXCART (SR-71, or Blackbird) project, over half of all UFO reports from the late 1950s through the 1960s were accounted for by manned reconnaissance flights.' Source: Haines, Studies in Intelligence, 1997
- **Tier 1 documented.** 'Air Force BLUE BOOK investigators aware of the secret U-2 flights tried to explain away such sightings by linking them to natural phenomena such as ice crystals and temperature inversions... They were careful, however, not to reveal the true cause of the sighting to the public.' Source: Haines, 'CIA's Role in the Study of UFOs, 1947-90'
- **Tier 1 documented.** 'CIA officials wanted knowledge of any Agency interest in the subject of flying saucers carefully restricted, noting not only that the Robertson panel report was classified but also that any mention of CIA sponsorship of the panel was forbidden.' Source: Gerald K. Haines, 'A Die-hard Issue: CIA's Role in the Study of UFOs, 1947-1990', Studies in Intelligence, 1997

## KLAS-TV (Las Vegas)

KLAS-TV (Las Vegas) is a institution on the board; board tier C, contextual, real and relevant, no direct programme linkage on the record yet; dates 1981; axes C0 A0 D2; 6 connections.

In one line: CBS affiliate, Channel 8.

### What it is

KLAS-TV is the Las Vegas station where George Knapp has worked as anchor and I-Team investigative reporter since 1981, apart from a break from 1991 to 1995. It is where the Bob Lazar interviews aired in May and November 1989, putting Area 51 into global consciousness, and it remains the institutional base from which Knapp has run four decades of UAP reporting. A local CBS affiliate in a desert market being the originating venue for the most durable claims in this field is itself a structural fact about where this story has been allowed to live.

## Minot AFB, North Dakota

Minot AFB, North Dakota is a location on the board; board tier B, documented channel and capability, programme role indicated but not yet nailed to a primary source; dates 1966 to 1975-11-11; axes C1 A2 D1; 6 connections.

In one line: SAC installation; 91st Strategic Missile Wing and 5th Bomb Wing; 1966 incursions, the 24 October 1968 B-52 case, and a named appearance in the CINCNORAD message of 11 November 1975.

### What it is

THE HUB WITH THE MOST INDEPENDENT DETECTION CHANNELS AND ONE UNRESOLVED NAMING PROBLEM. Minot Air Force Base, North Dakota, home of the 91st Strategic Missile Wing and the 5th Bomb Wing, is the convergence point for three separate episodes this board already carries in pieces without a place to hang them on: the 1966 incursions over its Minuteman launch facilities, the 24 October 1968 B-52 case, which is the best-instrumented nuclear-site incursion in the American record, and its named appearance in the CINCNORAD four-part message of 11 November 1975. THE NAMING PROBLEM IS REAL AND MUST NOT BE SILENTLY RESOLVED. For 10 November 1975 the 24th NORAD Region Senior Director's Log records a sighting at 'Minot Air Force Station', a radar site, and its own next clause says the object 'passed over the radar station'. Nine days later CINCNORAD's summary message lists 'Minot AFB, ND' among the installations where reliable military personnel had visually sighted suspicious objects. Two NORAD documents from the same period name two different Minot installations, and nothing opened by this board resolves which is meant. That matters for this hub specifically, because a degree count on l-minot that silently absorbs a radar-station entry is a degree count that lies.

### Why it holds its tier

Re-graded B on a global pass (rank 561 of 1159, score 29). 6 connections, 0 of them custody/funding/programmatic. Axes C1/A2/D1.

### The claims on the record

- **Tier 1 documented.** Seven airmen completed AF Form 117 questionnaires in 1968, which places their statements in the contemporaneous official record rather than in any later interview: A1C Lloyd M. Isley and A1C Robert Michael O'Connor of the 91st MIMS; A1C Joseph Patrick Jablonski, A1C Gregory Adams, SSgt James Frederick Bond and SSgt William E. Smith Jr. of the 862nd SPS; and Major James A. Partin, pilot, 23rd Bomb Squadron, 5th Bomb Wing. Source: https://minotb52ufo.com/doc.php, opened 2026-09-19
- **Tier 1 documented.** THE NAMING DISCREPANCY, STATED RATHER THAN RESOLVED. The 24th NORAD Region Senior Director's Log for 10 November 1975 reads: 'UFO sighting reported by Minot Air Force Station, a bright star-like object in the West, moving east, about the size of a car. First seen approximately 1015Z. Approximately 1120Z the object passed over the radar station, 1,000 feet to 2,000 feet high, no noise heard. Three people from the site or local area saw the object.' The CINCNORAD four-part message of 11 November 1975 instead lists 'Minot AFB, ND'. Minot Air Force Station is a radar site and is not the 91st Strategic Missile Wing's missile field. No opened record resolves which installation the 1975 sequence means. Source: 24th NORAD Region Senior Directors Log, 10 November 1975, https://archive.org/download/MalmstromAirForceBaseIncident/Malmstrom%20Air%20Force%20Base%20Incident%20%E2%80%93%20March%2016,%201967%20NORAD%20logs_djvu.txt ; CINCNORAD message of 11 November 1975 as excerpted at http://www.nicap.org/intsac.htm ; both opened 2026-09-19
- **Tier 1 documented.** The 24 October 1968 case generated a dense primary file: Project Blue Book's final case report of 13 November 1968, twelve pages; Basic Reporting Data of 28 October 1968, eight pages, prepared by Lt Col Arthur J. Werlich of the 862nd Combat Support Group Operations Division; the 91st Strategic Missile Wing Security Controller's summary listing UFO observers at Launch Control Facilities with sighting times; the Base Operations Dispatcher's Log for 0800 to 1010Z recording ground reports from site N-7; seven AF Form 117 witness questionnaires; thirteen B-52 ASQ-38 radarscope photographs with data plates; the Werlich overlay map at 1:200,000; and a transcription of recorded conversations between the B-52 co-pilot and Radar Approach Control. Source: Documentation index for the 24 October 1968 Minot AFB case, https://minotb52ufo.com/doc.php, opened 2026-09-19
- **Tier 2 named person on the record.** Minot is named in the CINCNORAD four-part message of 11 November 1975: 'Since 28 Oct 75 numerous reports of suspicious objects have been received at the NORAD CU; reliable military personnel at Loring AFB, Maine, Wurtsmith AFB, Michigan, Malmstrom AFB, Mt, Minot AFB, ND, and Canadian Forces Station, Falconbridge, Ontario, Canada have visually sighted suspicious objects.' Source: NICAP, http://www.nicap.org/intsac.htm, opened 2026-09-19

## Nevada Test Site / Nevada National Security Site

### What it is

The Nevada complex is where the classification regimes overlap. ## Los Alamos National Laboratory

Los Alamos National Laboratory is a institution on the board; board tier B, documented channel and capability, programme role indicated but not yet nailed to a primary source; dates 1943; axes C2 A3 D1; 6 connections.

In one line: DOE FFRDC administered by Triad National Security, LLC since 9 June 2018; Los Alamos, NM.

### What it is

Los Alamos is the first place the United States convened scientists to discuss unexplained objects over its own nuclear installations, and it is the laboratory that confirms it. On 16 February 1949 a conference was held at Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory on the green fireballs then appearing over the New Mexico weapons complex; attendees included Laboratory Director Norris Bradbury, Edward Teller and Frederick Reines, together with representatives of the FBI, the Atomic Energy Commission and the US military. LANL's own National Security Research Center published this in November 2024, stating that it holds the conference minutes, that its senior archivist receives several UFO-related FOIA requests every year, and that the Center does not appear to hold materials on Project Twinkle although not all of its millions of items are searchable. In December 1949 Project Twinkle was established as a network of observation and photographic stations and never fully implemented. Newly declassified records on the 1949 conference were publicised in July 2026 in the wake of the PURSUE releases. In April 2026, filmmaker Jeremy Corbell announced a trove of documents said to have been provided by the son of a deceased former LANL cybersecurity chief, forming the basis of the documentary 'Sleeping Dog' and alleged to include material on a secret 1991 UFO meeting at the laboratory. LANL is administered by Triad National Security, LLC and was funded at approximately 3,918.3 million dollars in FY2024 - the second-largest FFRDC in the country. It is a contractor-operated laboratory whose archives are not agency records, which is why a laboratory blog post is currently a better source on the 1949 conference than any FOIA response.

## MJ-12 / Operation Majestic-12 Documents

MJ-12 / Operation Majestic-12 Documents is a document on the board; board tier B, documented channel and capability, programme role indicated but not yet nailed to a primary source; dates 1984 to 1990; axes C1 A1 D2; 6 connections.

In one line: Purported 1952 Eisenhower briefing document and associated papers, surfaced 1984-1987.

### What it is

The MJ-12 corpus originates in a roll of undeveloped 35mm film that arrived anonymously, postmarked Albuquerque, at the Los Angeles home of television producer Jaime Shandera on 11 December 1984. Developed, it produced an eight-page 'Briefing Document: Operation Majestic 12' dated 18 November 1952, prepared for President-elect Eisenhower, naming twelve officials and describing the recovery of a crashed disc and four bodies near Roswell. Shandera, Bill Moore and Stanton Friedman released it publicly in May 1987. The National Archives searched Air Force, Joint Chiefs, NSC, Truman Library and Eisenhower Library holdings and found nothing except a single document in Record Group 341: the Cutler-Twining memorandum of 14 July 1954, whose problems NARA itself enumerated - no Top Secret register number, no letterhead or watermark, a security marking that NSC's FOIA office says post-dates the Eisenhower administration, and a paper stock ('diction onionskin') inconsistent with the Eisenhower Library's sample. The FBI investigated and states an Air Force investigation determined the document to be a fake. The board's position is that the MJ-12 documents are best understood not as evidence of a 1947 committee but as evidence of a 1980s operation: the Albuquerque postmark, the Doty and Moore connections, and the discovery of a planted-looking document inside a federal record group all point at the same place at the same time as the Bennewitz campaign.

## National Intelligence Program (NIP)

National Intelligence Program (NIP) is a program on the board; board tier B, documented channel and capability, programme role indicated but not yet nailed to a primary source; dates 2004-12-17; axes C1 A3 D2; 6 connections.

In one line: The non-DoD-controlled half of the US intelligence budget; funded across many agencies, controlled by the DNI.

### What it is

The National Intelligence Program is the intelligence budget that the Director of National Intelligence controls, as distinct from the Military Intelligence Program which the Secretary of Defense controls. Its aggregate appropriated total has been published annually since FY2007 under section 601 of the Implementing Recommendations of the 9/11 Commission Act of 2007 (Public Law 110-53), which requires the DNI to disclose the aggregate amount appropriated within thirty days of the end of each fiscal year; since February 2011 the aggregate request has also been published, under section 364 of the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2010. Those are the only two numbers Congress has required to be made public. The appropriated toplines run from $43.5 billion in FY2007 to $73.3 billion in FY2025, with an FY2026 request of $81.9 billion. What is not published is any breakdown whatsoever: not by agency, not by programme, not by intelligence discipline, not by appropriation account. The NIP is not itself an appropriation - it is a cross-cutting programme construct whose money is appropriated inside other bills and other departments' accounts, chiefly the Department of Defense, which is the structural fact that makes the intelligence budget a concealment mechanism rather than merely a secret. A dollar appropriated in a Department of Defense account, scored to the NIP, controlled by the DNI, and executed by a contractor is a dollar with four different institutional owners and one public number.

### Why it holds its tier

Re-graded B on a global pass (rank 188 of 1159, score 47). 6 connections, 3 of them custody/funding/programmatic. Axes C1/A3/D2.

### What it is

The central filing of the set and the one that produced the public controversy. Application 15/141270 was filed on 28 April 2016 from NAWCAD and granted on 4 December 2018, assigned to 'The United States of America as represented by the Secretary of the Navy'. ## The Roswell Report: Case Closed (1997)

The Roswell Report: Case Closed (1997) is a document on the board; board tier B, documented channel and capability, programme role indicated but not yet nailed to a primary source; dates 1997; axes C0 A2 D1; 6 connections.

In one line: HQ USAF / GPO, by Capt. James McAndrew; 231 pp.

### What it is

The second and more consequential official Air Force report, authored by James McAndrew and published by Headquarters United States Air Force through the Government Printing Office in 1997, addressing the alien-bodies claims that the 1994-1995 report had not covered. Its four stated conclusions are that Air Force activities spanning many years were consolidated into two or three days in July 1947; that the 'aliens' were probably anthropomorphic test dummies carried aloft by high-altitude balloons; that the 'unusual' military activity in the desert was balloon launch and recovery, with the units that always arrived shortly after a crash being accurate descriptions of dummy-recovery teams; and that the Roswell Army Air Field hospital bodies claims most likely combine a 1956 KC-97 crash killing eleven airmen with a 1959 manned balloon mishap injuring two pilots. The report also asserts flatly that 'the claims of bodies only became part of the Roswell Incident after 1978'. What makes it a first-order artifact rather than a press release is what it printed: anthropomorphic dummy launch and landing locations at Appendix A; sworn witness statements from ten named Air Force personnel at Appendix B including Col. Joseph W. Kittinger Jr., Col. Dan D. Fulgham, Bernard D. Gildenberg and Lt. Col. Raymond A. Madson; and full interview transcripts of five pro-UFO witnesses at Appendix C - Gerald Anderson, Glenn Dennis, Alice Knight, Vern Maltais and James Ragsdale, the Dennis interview supplied by its interviewer Karl T. Pflock. Section 2.1 is the most forensically detailed passage the US government has ever published on a UFO claim: it works the 427th AAF Base Unit Squadron 'M' morning reports and the National Personnel Records Center holdings to establish that Glenn Dennis's 'Naomi Maria Selff' never existed and to identify 1st Lt. Eileen M. Fanton as matching every other particular of his description.

### The board's reading

The most heavily documented artifact in the Roswell record, on either side. It prints the anthropomorphic dummy launch and landing locations, sworn statements from ten named Air Force personnel including Joseph W. Kittinger Jr., and full interview transcripts of the five principal pro-UFO witnesses. Its Section 2.1 nurse analysis is the only occasion on which the United States government has publicly worked a UFO witness claim down to certified daily personnel accounting records and named the individual it believes the witness actually described. Whatever one concludes about Project Mogul and the dummies, this is the standard of documentation this board holds every claim to, including the ones it finds persuasive.

### Why it holds its tier

Re-graded B on a global pass (rank 255 of 1159, score 42). 6 connections, 0 of them custody/funding/programmatic, 4 official denials recorded against it. Axes C0/A2/D1.

### The claims on the record

- **Tier 1 documented.** Appendix B of the report is a collection of signed sworn statements based on in-person interviews, including statements from Col. Charles A. Coltman Jr. USAF MC (Ret), Col. Dan D. Fulgham USAF (Ret) and Bernard D. Gildenberg GS-14 (Ret). Source: The Roswell Report: Case Closed (1997), Table of Contents / Appendix B; https://www.gutenberg.org/files/63659/63659-h/63659-h.htm
- **Tier 1 documented.** Appendix B prints sworn witness statements from Charles E. Clouthier, Col. Charles A. Coltman Jr., Col. Dan D. Fulgham, Bernard D. Gildenberg, MSgt Ole Jorgeson, Lt. Col. ## Acknowledged, unacknowledged and waived, the three states of a DoD SAP

Acknowledged, unacknowledged and waived, the three states of a DoD SAP is a domain on the board; board tier A, named in sworn testimony or primary documents as directly inside the programme; dates 2010-07-01; axes C2 A3 D3; 6 connections.

In one line: taxonomy.

### What it is

The three-state taxonomy is the vocabulary the whole board depends on, and it is defined word for word in DoD's own issuances. An ACKNOWLEDGED SAP is 'A SAP whose existence is acknowledged, affirmed, or made known to others, but its specific details (technologies, materials, techniques, etc.,) are classified as specified in the applicable SCG'. Its name appears in the budget; you may know that it exists and nothing else. An UNACKNOWLEDGED SAP is 'A SAP having enhanced security measures ensuring the existence of the program is not acknowledged, affirmed, or made known to any person not authorized for such information'. The correct response to an inquiry is neither confirmation nor denial; the program's very existence is classified. A WAIVED SAP is 'A SAP for which the SecDef has waived applicable reporting in accordance with Reference (c) following a determination of adverse effect to national security. An unacknowledged SAP that has more restrictive reporting and access controls than other unacknowledged SAPs' - Reference (c) being 10 U.S.C. 119. Cross-cutting the three states are three categories defined by mission: an acquisition SAP protects 'sensitive research, development, testing and evaluation, modification, and procurement activities'; an intelligence SAP protects intelligence activity; and an operations and support SAP is 'established primarily to protect the planning for, execution of, and support to especially sensitive military operations' and 'may protect organizations, property, operational concepts, plans, or activities'. A SAP with subordinate structure is called an 'umbrella', with 'compartments, sub-compartments, or projects' beneath it. The single most important observation for this board is that the alleged legacy recovery effort - if it exists - would sit precisely at the intersection of a waived unacknowledged operations and support SAP with an acquisition SAP for the exploitation work, held under an umbrella whose compartments are known only to the compartment holders. Every element of that description is an ordinary term of art in DoDI 5205.11.

### The board's reading

Terms of art, precisely, and why each one matters to the allegations. ACKNOWLEDGED: existence admitted, details classified. If a recovery program were acknowledged, its nickname would be in the annual report and the argument would be over. UNACKNOWLEDGED: 'enhanced security measures ensuring the existence of the program is not acknowledged, affirmed, or made known to any person not authorized'. This is the state in which a truthful official can decline to confirm or deny, and in which a denial issued by a press office staffed by people without access is a denial made in good faith by people who genuinely do not know. WAIVED: an unacknowledged SAP whose statutory reporting has been removed by the Secretary. This is the state in which the phrase 'Congress was not informed' can be simultaneously true and lawful. Cross-cutting these are the mission categories - acquisition, intelligence, and operations and support, the last defined to protect 'the planning for, execution of, and support to especially sensitive military operations' and expressly capable of protecting 'organizations, property, operational concepts, plans, or activities'. The word 'property' in an official DoD definition is the closest thing in the public policy corpus to a category designed for custody of a physical object whose existence is itself the secret. And any SAP with subordinate structure is an 'umbrella' with 'compartments, sub-compartments, or projects' - which is why a person read into one compartment can truthfully testify to what he was told about others without ever having seen a document.

### Why it holds its tier

Re-graded A on a global pass (rank 67 of 1159, score 73). 6 connections, 4 of them custody/funding/programmatic, 1 official denial recorded against it. Axes C2/A3/D3.

### The claims on the record

- **Tier 1 documented.** DoDD 5205.07 (2010) Glossary: 'acquisition SAP. A SAP established to protect sensitive research, development, testing and evaluation, modification, and procurement activities.' Source: DoDD 5205.07 (2010), Glossary Part II

## SRI International (Stanford Research Institute)

SRI International (Stanford Research Institute) is a institution on the board; board tier B, documented channel and capability, programme role indicated but not yet nailed to a primary source; dates 1946; axes C1 A3 D2; 6 connections.

In one line: Independent nonprofit research institute; host of the CIA/DIA psychoenergetics programme 1972-1990.

### What it is

SRI was the private vehicle through which the United States ran a compartmented human-intelligence-collection experiment for nearly two decades without acknowledging it. Spun out of Stanford University, SRI held large volumes of classified defence work; from 1972 its Radio Physics Laboratory hosted Harold Puthoff and Russell Targ's psychoenergetics programme, funded initially by CIA's Office of Technical Service and later by Army INSCOM and DIA under successive codenames. The arrangement is the archetype this board tracks: a nonprofit research institute with a security apparatus, a government sponsor with deniability, published open-literature output where convenient (Nature, October 1974) and a classified programme record that took until 1995 to declassify. When the programme was finally exposed to independent evaluation and terminated, the personnel did not leave the field - Puthoff went on to the Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin, then NIDS, then BAASS, then To The Stars Academy. SRI is where the template of government-funded, privately-housed, unacknowledged anomalous research was proven to work.

## UFO Crash/Retrieval Status Reports I-VII (Stringfield, 1978-1994)

UFO Crash/Retrieval Status Reports I-VII (Stringfield, 1978-1994) is a document on the board; board tier C, contextual, real and relevant, no direct programme linkage on the record yet; dates 1978-07-29 to 1994-02; axes C0 A0 D3; 6 connections.

In one line: Seven-part self-published monograph series, 1978-1994.

### What it is

The seven UFO Crash/Retrieval Status Reports written by Leonard H. Stringfield between 1978 and 1994 are the founding corpus of the crash-retrieval literature and the reason the subject exists as a research field rather than as folklore. Status Report I is 'Retrievals of the Third Kind: A Case Study of Alleged UFOs and Occupants in Military Custody', delivered as a paper at the ninth annual MUFON Symposium in Dayton, Ohio on 29 July 1978 (revised 20 July 1978) and published in Flying Saucer Review; it grew out of the informant response to Stringfield's 1977 Doubleday book 'Situation Red, The UFO Siege'. Status Report II, 'The UFO Crash/Retrieval Syndrome: New Sources, New Data', is dated January 1980 and was published by MUFON; it introduced the letter-number case coding (Cases A-1 onward, Items B-1 onward) that structures the whole series, and included the first Del Rio and Wright-Patterson entries. Status Report III, 'Amassing the Evidence' (1982), carried endorsements from Dr. Peter Rank, Chief of Radiology at Methodist Hospital, and Richard H. Hall, former Assistant Director of NICAP and editor of the MUFON UFO Journal, and printed a consolidated chronology of every case reported in Status Report II - the field's first tabulated retrieval index. Status Report IV, 'The Fatal Encounter at Ft. Dix-McGuire: A Case Study' (June 1985), is a single-case monograph on an alleged 18 January 1978 incident at McGuire AFB and Fort Dix, developed from a USAF Security Police sergeant who had first appeared as Case A3 in Report III, and opens with a prologue titled 'The Burden of Proof' in which Stringfield states that public research does not possess proof and that affidavits, leaked documents and photographs are not proof. Status Report V, 'Is the Coverup Lid Lifting?' (January 1989), surveys Roswell, Aztec, Kingman, El Yunque and Brown County, Ohio, and argues that confirming any single retrieval would compel eventual sharing of alien propulsion and materials technology. Status Report VI, 'The Inner Sanctum' (July 1991), was self-published from 4412 Grove Avenue, Cincinnati, edited by Richard Hall and typed by Chris Coffey, and opens with the Humpty Dumpty verse from Through the Looking Glass. Status Report VII, 'Search for Proof in a Hall of Mirrors' (February 1994), acknowledges funding from the Fund for UFO Research and cooperation from MUFON, CUFOS and the Mid-Ohio Research Associates, opens with Walter Scott's 'I cannot tell how the truth may be; I say the tale as 'twas told to me', and closes the series ten months before Stringfield's death with a Roswell crash/retrieval update noting a source's placement of the site north of Roswell rather than on the Plains of San Augustin. The series' method - anonymous sources behind letter-number codes - is simultaneously the reason the material exists and the reason almost none of it can be graded above tier 2.

### The board's reading

The seven Status Reports are the domain's founding corpus and its founding problem. Dated and titled precisely: I, 'Retrievals of the Third Kind', MUFON Symposium, Dayton, 29 July 1978 (revised 20 July 1978), also published in Flying Saucer Review; II, 'The UFO Crash/Retrieval Syndrome: New Sources, New Data', January 1980, published by MUFON; III, 'Amassing the Evidence', 1982, endorsed by Dr. Peter Rank of Methodist Hospital and Richard H. Hall, former Assistant Director of NICAP; IV, 'The Fatal Encounter at Ft. Dix-McGuire', June 1985; V, 'Is the Coverup Lid Lifting?', January 1989; VI, 'The Inner Sanctum', July 1991, self-published at 4412 Grove Avenue, Cincinnati, edited by Richard Hall; VII, 'Search for Proof in a Hall of Mirrors', February 1994. Complete scans of all seven are public. The corpus is the reason the crash-retrieval field exists and the reason it cannot be audited: the source-protection coding that made it possible to collect made it impossible to check.

### Why it holds its tier

Re-graded C on a global pass (rank 789 of 1159, score 22). 6 connections, 0 of them custody/funding/programmatic. Axes C0/A0/D3.

## University at Albany (SUNY), Department of Physics

University at Albany (SUNY), Department of Physics is a institution on the board; board tier B, documented channel and capability, programme role indicated but not yet nailed to a primary source; dates 2005; axes C0 A1 D2; 6 connections.

In one line: Academic home of Kevin Knuth and Matthew Szydagis; institutional base of UAPx.

### What it is

CORRECTED NODE - description updated to add Cecilia Levy, the second 2025 paper, and the departmental research-interest listing. The physics department at the University at Albany is, improbably, the most productive academic base in this field outside Stanford and Harvard. It employs Kevin Knuth - information physicist, former NASA Ames research scientist and Editor-in-Chief of Entropy since 2012, on the faculty since 2005 and a full professor since 2023 - along with Matthew Szydagis, a liquid-xenon dark-matter physicist who created the Noble Element Simulation Technique used across the direct-detection community, and Cecilia Levy, an LZ physicist and Szydagis's co-developer on the Snowball Chamber. What makes the institution more than an address is that the commitment is on the record in the department's own materials: Szydagis's faculty page lists 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena' among his research interests, and the University's news office published the June 2025 field results under its own masthead, naming the three as 'UAlbany authors' and reporting the honest outcome that the team 'succeeded in plausibly explaining all but one of the potential anomalies detected'. Two papers came out of the same Progress in Aerospace Sciences special edition: the UAPx field-expedition results and Knuth's 34-author review, 'The New Science of Unidentified Aerospace-Undersea Phenomena (UAP)'. Knuth also produced the 2019 Entropy kinematics paper on the Nimitz encounter, and in June 2025 received SCU's inaugural Distinguished Scholar Award. That a mid-sized state university supplies a meaningful fraction of the world's peer-reviewed UAP instrumentation output is a measure of how little institutional capacity exists. Note that UAlbany is not the host or funder of UAPx - the field work was funded by Caroline Cory of OMnium Media for the documentary 'A Tear in the Sky' (2022).

## The Aerospace Corporation

The Aerospace Corporation is a institution on the board; board tier B, documented channel and capability, programme role indicated but not yet nailed to a primary source; dates 1960; axes C2 A3 D1; 5 connections.

In one line: Nonprofit operator of the Aerospace FFRDC for the US Space Force; El Segundo, CA; founded 1960.

### What it is

Aerospace is the FFRDC that owns the technical judgement on everything the United States puts into, or detects from, orbit - and it is the second named target of the congressional inquiry. It was created in 1960 at the Air Force's insistence, announced by Lt. Gen. Bernard Schriever, to provide dedicated scientific and technical planning for the military space and ballistic missile programmes after the conflict-of-interest problems of the earlier Ramo-Wooldridge arrangement. Congress's Office of Technology Assessment noted in its 1995 history of DoD FFRDCs that the Air Force insisted on specific restrictions in the Aerospace charter that it had not imposed elsewhere - the government designed this one to be structurally constrained precisely because it would sit at the centre of national security space. Today Aerospace operates the only FFRDC committed exclusively to the space enterprise, with roughly 4,800 employees, funded at approximately 1,309.8 million dollars in FY2024, under Space Force contract FA880219C0001 recorded on USAspending at approximately 8.67 billion dollars over 2018-2028. Its relevance to this board is direct: any persistent orbital or transmedium object detected by national security space sensors would be characterised technically by Aerospace, not by the Space Force in-house, and Aerospace also performs system engineering and integration for NNSA's Defense Nuclear Nonproliferation and Defense Programs offices under DOE contract 89233120CNA000134. Rep. Burlison has named Aerospace explicitly among the organisations his investigation is following, and Ross Coulthart has publicly raised Aerospace and MITRE in connection with the 2026 UAP Governance Board. No document has been produced placing Aerospace in a legacy programme. What is documented is that it holds the technical keys to the space sensor picture and that Congress has now put it on the list.

## Armed Forces Special Weapons Project

Armed Forces Special Weapons Project is a institution on the board; board tier B, documented channel and capability, programme role indicated but not yet nailed to a primary source; dates 1946-12-31 to 1959-05-06; axes C2 A3 D1; 5 connections.

In one line: Joint Army-Navy atomic energy organisation, 1946-1959; military successor to the Manhattan Engineer District.

### What it is

The Armed Forces Special Weapons Project was established by joint directive of the Secretaries of War and the Navy, effective midnight 31 December 1946, to carry on the military service functions of the Manhattan Project that were retained under armed forces control when the Atomic Energy Commission took the civil ones. It reported directly to the Army Chief of Staff and the Chief of Naval Operations, its Chief and Deputy Chief sat on the Military Liaison Committee to the AEC, and its funds came by working fund advances from the AEC out of money formerly available to the Manhattan Project. Major General Leslie R. Groves became its first Chief on 28 February 1947. It was redesignated the Defense Atomic Support Agency in 1959 and, through DNA and DSWA, is the ancestor of the Defense Threat Reduction Agency.

### Why it holds its tier

Re-graded B on a global pass (rank 183 of 1159, score 47). 5 connections, 1 of them custody/funding/programmatic. Axes C2/A3/D1.

### The claims on the record

- **Tier 1 documented.** AFSWP took the military half of the Manhattan Project. The charter makes it 'responsible for carrying on the military service functions of the Manhattan Project retained under control of the armed forces', including military participation in the development of atomic weapons of all types in coordination with the Atomic Energy Commission, and assigns to it as of 31 December 1946 the Army units that had been assigned to the Manhattan Engineer District. Source: War Department Memorandum No. 850-25-8, paras. 2, 3 and 5, in Defense's Nuclear Agency 1947-1997, Appendix D, https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA412977/DTIC_ADA412977_djvu.txt
- **Tier 1 documented.** Groves held the command for one year to the day. The Defense Threat Reduction Agency's chronology of its own lineage reads: 'Feb. 28, 1947. Maj Gen Groves becomes first Chief AFSWP, serving for one year, until his retirement on February 29, 1948; he is promoted to Lt. General on January 24, 1948.' The same history records that the command stood empty when it was created: 'between the beginning of January and the end of February 1947, there was no officially appointed chief of AFSWP. During this period, Groves' aide, Colonel Hasbrouck, assumed Headquarters command in Washington as the senior officer of the organization.' Source: Defense's Nuclear Agency 1947-1997, Defense Threat Reduction Agency, 2002, Appendix C: Chronology, DTIC ADA412977, https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA412977/DTIC_ADA412977_djvu.txt

## Bolender Memorandum

Bolender Memorandum is a document on the board; board tier B, documented channel and capability, programme role indicated but not yet nailed to a primary source; dates 1969; axes C1 A3 D3; 5 connections.

In one line: Brig. Gen. C. H. Bolender, 20 October 1969.

### What it is

The memorandum by Brig. Gen. Carroll H. Bolender, USAF Deputy Director of Development, dated 20 October 1969, recommending termination of Project Blue Book. Its historical importance is not the recommendation but the justification. Bolender explains that reports of unidentified flying objects which could affect national security are made in accordance with JANAP 146 or Air Force Manual 55-11 and are not part of the Blue Book system, and therefore that terminating Blue Book would not affect the Air Force's ability to handle national-security cases. That is an official written statement that the program the public believed was the government's UFO investigation had never handled the cases that mattered. The memo also observes that the retention of Blue Book records would not be a problem once the project ended, and Blue Book's holdings duly went to the National Archives while whatever accumulated on the JANAP side has never been identified as a records series, never been accessioned, and never been searched. Two months after Bolender wrote, Secretary of the Air Force Robert C. Seamans Jr. announced Blue Book's closure on 17 December 1969, citing the Condon Report.

### The board's reading

The Bolender memorandum is short, administrative, and the most quietly damaging document in the legacy corpus. Its purpose was to justify closing Project Blue Book, and its argument was that closure would cost the Air Force nothing operationally because the reports that mattered had never been in Blue Book to begin with: UFO reports which could affect national security were made in accordance with JANAP 146 or Air Force Manual 55-11, and were not part of the Blue Book system. Read against JANAP 146(C) of 10 March 1954, which made unidentified flying objects a mandatory CIRVIS report and prohibited unauthorised disclosure of report contents under 18 U.S.C. 793 and 794, the memo describes a two-track structure operating for at least fifteen years: a public program that generated 12,618 catalogued sightings and a residue of 701 unknowns, and a classified channel whose output has never been named as a records series, never been accessioned by the National Archives, and never been searched under any disclosure statute, including the FY2024 NDAA provisions that created Record Group 615. Blue Book's records went to College Park. The other channel's records went somewhere that has not been identified in fifty-seven years. That gap is the specific, concrete, documentable thing this board exists to track, and it was opened by a brigadier general writing routine staff correspondence, not by a whistleblower.

### Why it holds its tier

Re-graded B on a global pass (rank 193 of 1159, score 46). 5 connections, 3 of them custody/funding/programmatic, 1 official denial recorded against it. Axes C1/A3/D3.

### The claims on the record

- **Tier 1 documented.** The memorandum is dated 20 October 1969 and signed by Brig. Gen. C. H. Bolender, USAF Deputy Director of Development. Source: Bolender memorandum, 20 Oct 1969 (archived scan)
- **Tier 2 named person on the record.** The memorandum states that reports of unidentified flying objects which could affect national security are made under JANAP 146 or AFM 55-11 and 'are not part of the Blue Book system'. Source: Bolender memorandum, 20 Oct 1969, as quoted throughout the literature; the archived scan is an untranscribed image
- **Tier 3 stated inference.** No records series corresponding to the JANAP 146 national-security UFO reports has ever been identified, accessioned by NARA, or searched under any subsequent disclosure statute. ## Prime Contractor Custody

Prime Contractor Custody is a domain on the board; board tier B, documented channel and capability, programme role indicated but not yet nailed to a primary source; dates 1947-01-01; axes C3 A3 D1; 5 connections.

In one line: Industrial domain - the private firms alleged to hold material, and the legal shelter that creates.

### What it is

Moving a programme into a prime contractor does not merely add secrecy - it changes the legal category of everything inside it. Contractor records are not agency records and so fall outside the Freedom of Information Act; contractor facilities are inspected by the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency rather than by congressional staff; and proprietary data markings restrict government-side circulation independently of classification. GAO reported in 2004 that DoD could not provide adequate assurance that its industrial security oversight was protecting classified information at contractor facilities - a finding about the mechanism's opacity from the government's own auditor. This is the structural reason the custody question and the contractor question are the same question: an object on a contractor's shelf is legally further from Congress than the same object on a government shelf, without any change in its classification. The named firms recur across sworn and named-source testimony rather than across documents, which is precisely why this domain is scored on the C axis and researched through contract data, facility clearance records and personnel movement. Scoring high here means an entity is alleged to hold material or to have managed those who do.

### Why it holds its tier

## Special Access Programs

Special Access Programs is a domain on the board; board tier B, documented channel and capability, programme role indicated but not yet nailed to a primary source; dates 1960-01-01; axes C2 A3 D2; 5 connections.

In one line: Access-control domain - the SAP/USAP/waived tier and its oversight carve-outs.

### What it is

A special access programme is the mechanism by which the executive branch creates an information space with tighter controls than Top Secret and a smaller list of people who may enter it. The tier structure is documented policy, not speculation: acknowledged SAPs whose existence is public though their content is not; unacknowledged SAPs whose very existence is classified; and waived unacknowledged SAPs for which the Secretary of Defense has exercised the 10 U.S.C. 119 waiver so that notification runs only to the chairs and ranking members of the armed services and defence appropriations committees - eight members, typically without staff, typically orally. That last category is the load-bearing one for this board, because it is a lawful configuration in which a programme can run for decades while the overwhelming majority of Congress has no lawful means of learning it exists. In 2009 the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence prepared an information memorandum reviewing a request to convert DIA's advanced aerospace work into a special access programme - a documented instance of the transition being considered for exactly this subject matter. Scoring high on this domain means an entity held, granted, or was formally denied SAP-level access, and the denial is scored as heavily as the grant.

### Why it holds its tier

## Secrecy Law & Classification

Secrecy Law & Classification is a domain on the board; board tier B, documented channel and capability, programme role indicated but not yet nailed to a primary source; dates 1946-08-01; axes C1 A3 D1; 5 connections.

In one line: Legal domain - the statutory and executive machinery that makes concealment lawful.

### What it is

Everything this board describes is, on its face, legal - and that is the point. Classification authority flows from executive order rather than statute for most national security information, which means the same executive branch that runs a programme also decides whether Congress and the courts may learn of it. Layered on top are the Atomic Energy Act's 'born classified' Restricted Data regime, the Invention Secrecy Act's power to impose secrecy orders on patent applications, and 50 U.S.C. 3510's authority for unvouchered and confidential expenditure certified by agency heads rather than audited. The dual-use route into a concealment programme is simple and requires no conspiracy: an activity placed inside a special access programme, then waived from ordinary congressional notification under the exception in 10 U.S.C. 119, is protected by exactly the same machinery whether it holds a stealth aircraft or a recovered craft, and the machinery cannot tell the difference. Scoring high on this domain means an entity is a wielder of classification authority - an original classification authority, a security officer, a programme security manager - rather than a person subject to it.

### Why it holds its tier

Re-graded B on a global pass (rank 454 of 1159, score 32). 5 connections, 1 of them custody/funding/programmatic. Axes C1/A3/D1.

### The claims on the record

- **Tier 1 documented.** 10 U.S.C. 119 requires congressional notification of special access programmes but permits the Secretary of Defense to waive that notification for a programme, reporting instead only to the chairs and ranking members of the defence committees. Source: 10 U.S.C. Sec. 119, Special access programs: congressional oversight
- **Tier 1 documented.** 50 U.S.C. 3510 permits certain intelligence expenditures to be accounted for solely on the certificate of the agency head, with that certificate deemed a sufficient voucher. Source: 50 U.S.C. 3510 (Cornell LII)
- **Tier 1 documented.** DoD Directive 5205.07 establishes the policy framework for acknowledged, unacknowledged and waived special access programmes and assigns the approval authority. Source: DoD Directive 5205.07, Special Access Program (SAP) Policy

The data that could resolve most of this exists, and it is classified for reasons that have nothing to do with the objects. Radar tracks, infrared imagery, electronic intelligence collection and measurement and signature intelligence are protected because releasing them reveals sensor sensitivity, coverage geometry and collection technique - the classic sources-and-methods problem - which means the government can be entirely sincere in withholding material that would also settle a public controversy. The National Security Agency's posture is the documented extreme: in Citizens Against UFO Secrecy v. NSA the courts sustained withholding of the substance of the agency's UFO-related holdings on the strength of the classified Yeates affidavit, and the released material is heavily redacted. The institutional convergence became explicit in August 2024, when a senior NSA researcher, Jon Kosloski, was appointed to lead AARO - placing a signals-intelligence technologist at the head of the office responsible for the government's UAP analysis. Congress has pushed on the same seam, requiring reporting on military intercepts over North America in the FY2026 NDAA cycle. Scoring high on this domain means an entity collected, held or adjudicated release of sensor data.

## Defense Appropriations Acts FY2008 and FY2010, the $22M AAWSAP appropriation

Defense Appropriations Acts FY2008 and FY2010, the $22M AAWSAP appropriation is a legislation on the board; board tier B, documented channel and capability, programme role indicated but not yet nailed to a primary source; dates 2007 to 2012; axes C0 A3 D2; 5 connections.

In one line: Classified annex appropriation directed by Senate leadership.

### What it is

The funding instrument, and the reason the whole thing stayed invisible. AARO's own history states that 'at the direction of Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid (D-NV), the Defense Appropriations Acts of Fiscal Years 2008 and 2010 appropriated $22 million for the DIA to assess long-term and over-the-horizon foreign advanced aerospace threats.' The money was placed in the classified annex with the agreement of Appropriations chairman Daniel Inouye and senior Republican Ted Stevens, which meant it never appeared in a public budget justification, was never authorised by the Armed Services Committees, and was never subject to floor debate. The structural consequence runs through the entire modern disclosure fight: a program can be created, staffed, contracted and terminated over ten years using appropriated funds without the authorizing committees ever seeing it, and the only reason this one surfaced is that a newspaper published a story in December 2017 and DIA then had to write the Senate Armed Services Committee a letter explaining what it had been doing. The specific bill language and account line have never been released.

### Why it holds its tier

Re-graded B on a global pass (rank 298 of 1159, score 39). 5 connections, 5 of them custody/funding/programmatic. Axes C0/A3/D2.

## United States Department of Homeland Security

United States Department of Homeland Security is a institution on the board; board tier A, named in sworn testimony or primary documents as directly inside the programme; dates 2002-11-25; axes C2 A3 D2; 5 connections.

In one line: Cabinet department created 2002; the department that stood up and then killed KONA BLUE.

### What it is

DHS was established in 2002, 'combining 22 different federal departments and agencies into a unified, integrated Cabinet agency' with more than 260,000 employees, and its Office of Intelligence and Analysis is a full element of the Intelligence Community. For most of its existence DHS had no visible role in the UAP question. That changed with the declassification of KONA BLUE. According to the joint AARO/DHS paper 'History and Origin of KONA BLUE', KONA BLUE was 'a Prospective Special Access Program (PSAP) that had been proposed to DHS leadership but was never approved or formally established'; in 2011 the DHS Under Secretary for Science and Technology established KONA BLUE as a PSAP, and approximately six months later the DHS Deputy Secretary disapproved and terminated it. AARO's Historical Record Report Volume I states that after DIA cancelled AAWSAP/AATIP in 2012 'its supporters proposed to DHS that they create and fund a new version' to 'restart UAP investigations, paranormal research (including alleged human consciousness anomalies) and reverse-engineer any recovered off-world spacecraft', that interviewees claimed KONA BLUE 'was a sensitive DHS compartment to cover up the retrieval and exploitation of non-human biologics', and that 'Senators Lieberman and Reid asked that the PSAP be established with the promise of additional funding'. AARO's reading is that KONA BLUE proves the recovery narrative was a proposal that got rejected; the opposite reading, which the same document supports, is that a compartment to hold recovered non-human material was requested at Under Secretary level, formally stood up as a prospective program, and killed only when it reached the Deputy Secretary. DHS is also, per AARO, one of the three special access program control office enterprises - DoD, IC and DHS - with which AARO says it partnered to review named programs.

## Disclosure Project witness cohort (68 testimonies, 2000 to 2001)

Disclosure Project witness cohort (68 testimonies, 2000 to 2001) is a institution on the board; board tier B, documented channel and capability, programme role indicated but not yet nailed to a primary source; dates 2000-07 to 2001-05-09; axes C0 A0 D3; 5 connections.

In one line: A SET NODE, NOT AN ORGANISATION. Carries the 68 named testimonies printed in section 3.8 of the April 2001 Briefing Document, and holds the witnesses for whom no independent record exists rather than giving each a single-claim node.

### What it is

THIS IS A SET NODE AND NOT AN ORGANISATION; NOTHING HERE EVER MET AS A BODY. It exists because a person node built on one testimony in one interested-party document would assert that somebody said something and nothing else, and because sixty-eight of those would make `witness-chain` the dominant edge type of an entire region of this board, which CLAUDE.md section 6 warns turns degree into a measure of how much is claimed rather than of what is true. The set carries the roster and the counts, and individual witnesses are promoted out of it only when an independent record is found, which in this pass happened for John Callahan, Clifford Stone, Robert Jacobs and Larry Warren and did not happen for Karl Wolfe, Donna Hare, Don Phillips or John Weygandt. Those four are held here with their claims and with the specific documentary problems each carries: Wolfe's NSA-at-Langley account against NASA's own record that the Lunar Orbiter programme was run by NASA Langley Research Center; Hare's employer documented by Ford Motor Company while her employment is documented nowhere; Phillips with nothing independent at all; and Weygandt, whose name the Briefing Document prints as John while the modern literature calls him Jonathan, which is precisely the class of error this board keeps having to undo.

### Why it holds its tier

Re-graded B on a global pass (rank 301 of 1159, score 39). 5 connections, 0 of them custody/funding/programmatic. Axes C0/A0/D3.

The editorial header states that he 'worked with Kelly Johnson at the Lockheed Skunkworks on design and construction of the U-2 and the SR-71 Blackbird'. In his own words the sighting was at 'Angels Peak... a classified radar installation', 'in 1966, to 67', with estimated speeds of '3,800 to 4,200 miles per hour equivalent, ground speed', and one named corroborating witness, 'a buddy that was chief radar operator named Anthony Kasar'. ## Relatório de Ocorrências, Comando Aéreo de Defesa Aérea, 2 June 1986 (Arquivo Nacional BR_DFANBSB_ARX_0_0_0249)

Relatório de Ocorrências, Comando Aéreo de Defesa Aérea, 2 June 1986 (Arquivo Nacional BR_DFANBSB_ARX_0_0_0249) is a document on the board; board tier B, documented channel and capability, programme role indicated but not yet nailed to a primary source; dates 1986-06-02 to 2009-09-25; axes C1 A2 D3; 5 connections.

In one line: CONFIDENCIAL Brazilian Air Defence Command report; declassified 25 September 2009.

### What it is

An eight-page document on Ministério da Aeronáutica letterhead, stamped CONFIDENCIAL on every page, addressed by the Commander of the Air Defence Air Command to the Commander General of the Air, dated Brasília-DF, 2 June 1986, signed by Brigadeiro do Ar José Pessoa Cavalcanti de Albuquerque as acting commander COMDA/NuCOMDABRA, and annexed with a Relatório de Ocorrências. It is scanned and served publicly by the Brazilian National Archives under reference BR_DFANBSB_ARX_0_0_0249 and was declassified on 25 September 2009, twenty-three years after the minister of aeronautics promised a full dossier within thirty days. Its section IV, Considerações Finais, is the operative text: it lists six behavioural characteristics observed and then states the Command's own opinion that the phenomena are solid and reflect a form of intelligence. It also praises the response posture, noting that each engaged air unit maintained an alert aircraft at 45 minutes' readiness and that within under thirty minutes of activation armed vectors were available. It is a document in which a national air defence command tells its own chain of command, in writing and under classification, that it has tracked solid, intelligently behaving unidentified objects that outran supersonic interceptors.

### Why it holds its tier

Re-graded B on a global pass (rank 323 of 1159, score 38). 5 connections, 3 of them custody/funding/programmatic. Axes C1/A2/D3.

### The claims on the record

- **Tier 1 documented.** Considerações Finais para 3: the Command's opinion that the phenomena 'são sólidos e refletem de certa forma inteligência ... não forçosamente tripulados'. Source: Arquivo Nacional BR_DFANBSB_ARX_0_0_0249
- **Tier 1 documented.** Document header: 'MINISTÉRIO DA AERONÁUTICA, COMANDO AÉREO DE DEFESA AÉREA ... Brasília-DF, 02 de Junho de 1986. Do Comandante. Ao Exmo Sr Comandante do Comando Geral do Ar. Assunto: Relatório de Ocorrência.' Classification marking [CONFIDENCIAL] on each page. Source: Arquivo Nacional BR_DFANBSB_ARX_0_0_0249, page images
- **Tier 2 named person on the record.** The report was released on 25 September 2009. Source: BBC Brasil, 14 January 2022; Wikipedia '1986 Brazilian UFO incident'
